description: Track I I2.4/I2.5/I4.5: invariants as candidate homomorphisms, wall explanations that name why an invented family cannot finish a task, the cheapest wall-breaking held process, and structural proof certificates for family invariants.

microtheory.name: invariant_miner
microtheory.description: Explain a wall by an invariant before fighting it.

attrs.name: det_sign
attrs.note: data only: no matrix domain is in PMB v1 yet

rules.name: im_parity_of_schema
rules.comment: I2.4: compute the perm_parity homomorphism of every permutation schema.

rules.name: im_preserves_parity
rules.comment: I2.4: an even permutation preserves the parity of every state it acts on.

rules.name: im_explain_parity_wall
rules.comment: I2.5: a stuck task whose state and goal differ in parity, in a domain whose every invented process is even, cannot be finished by the invented family. Name the wall.

rules.name: im_break_parity_wall
rules.comment: I2.5: break the wall with the cheapest held process that changes the invariant (an odd permutation), then resume solving.

rules.name: im_wall_unbreakable
rules.comment: I2.5: no held process changes the invariant; the wall stands (reported, not fought).

rules.name: im_proof_commutator_even
rules.comment: I4.5 certificate step: a commutator [a,b] is even for any a, b (parity is a homomorphism into the abelian group Z2).

rules.name: im_proof_conjugate_preserves
rules.comment: I4.5 certificate step: a conjugate s·t·s⁻¹ has the parity of t; it is proven even when t is a held process of exact parity 0 or t is itself proven even.

rules.name: im_family_parity_law
rules.comment: I4.5: when every active invented process in a permutation domain carries the structural certificate, promote 'the invented family is even' to a proven law.
